kh:body.kh:mini-summary: This Checklist contains a task list to assist all types of SM&CR firms comply with the Senior Managers and Certification Regime (SM&CR), including: the Senior Managers Regime (SMR); the Certification Regime; fitness and propriety requirements and criminal records checks; the FS Register of Senior Managers and Directory Persons; Regulatory References; Conduct Rules; and a task list for individual Senior Managers.
kh:body.core:para: NOTE: On 15 July 2025, the government announced the Leeds Reforms, which include plans to streamline the SM&CR. At the same time, the PRA and FCA published consultation papers CP18/25 and CP25/21. The regulators propose a two-stage reform process, with Phase Two to follow pending legislative changes under HM Treasury consultation. Final Phase One requirements are expected in mid-2026, with future Phase Two consultations dependent on HMT legislation. See News Analysis: Reform of the SM&CR—Proposals and next steps.

tr:secmain.core:title: Overview
tr:secmain.core:para: The Senior Managers and Certification Regime (SM&CR) is the UK financial services regulatory framework for regulating individuals working in financial services; the SM&CR aims to expand the scope of individual liability, focusing on senior management responsibility and creating a firm-wide ‘culture of accountability’ in order to reduce consumer harm and strengthen market integrity. The component parts of the SM&CR are the Senior Managers Regime (SMR), the Certification Regime and the Conduct Rules. The SMR aims to ensure that Senior Managers can be held liable for any misconduct that falls within their remit of responsibilities, while the Certification Regime and Conduct Rules intend to hold individuals working at all levels in financial services to suitable standards of conduct. For an introduction to the SM&CR, see: SM&CR—one minute guide.

The following task lists should assist firms in complying with the SM&CR. Enhanced Scope SM&CR firms, SM&CR Banking firms and certain SM&CR Insurance firms have more onerous compliance requirements than Core and Limited Scope SM&CR firms; therefore the task list below should be read in conjunction with the sector specific SM&CR practical guidance, set out in: SM&CR and approved persons regime—overview. Those additional tasks which apply only to Enhanced Scope SM&CR firms, SM&CR Banking firms and certain SM&CR Insurance firms are set out in italics.

row.entry: Ensure all SMFs relevant to the firm or indeed required of the firm, are identified, appropriately allocated and remain so; a list of relevant SMFs is set out in sector specific SM&CR Practice Notes which can be found in: SM&CR and approved persons regime—overview

Ensure all Senior Managers are approved by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and, where necessary, the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA); for more information see Practice Note: SM&CR—applications to perform SMFs, notifications, and withdrawal of approval

Note that the SM&CR applies at legal entity level, not group level, therefore, ensure Senior Managers have separate approvals to perform SMFs at each legal entity within a group structure; whomever is accountable for discharging a function in the regulated firm should hold the appropriate SMF, even if that individual is employed at group level rather than as an employee of the regulated firm

Note that the SMR has no territorial limit, geographical location is irrelevant—therefore, ensure that anyone performing a Senior Manager role exercising responsibilities over a UK entity is approved to perform the relevant SMF

entry.core:emph: Ensure there are no gaps in responsibility—delegate responsibility to a Senior Manager for every area, business activity and management function of the firm in order to comply with the FCA’s ‘Overall Responsibility’ requirement in SYSC 26. The FCA has not set out best practice guidance as to how firms map Overall Responsibility, it has set out steps firm may wish to consider in paragraph 8.27 of

row.entry: Reflect the SMF clearly in the Senior Manager’s Statement of Responsibilities (see below)
Check the Financial Services Register to ensure Senior Managers hold the correct approvals; for any necessary changes, see Practice Note: The Financial Services Register

Where a Senior Manager’s absence is temporary or reasonably unforeseen, someone may cover for that SMF and/or the absent Senior Manager’s responsibilities under the ‘Overall Responsibility’ requirement without being approved, where the appointment is for less than 12 consecutive weeks
Train Senior Managers in the scope, obligations and personal accountability of the SMR
Perform fitness and propriety assessments of Senior Managers at the point of recruitment or prior to the individual performing a SMF; see Fitness and propriety below
Perform annual fitness and propriety assessments of Senior Managers
Request and provide regulatory references for SMF candidates; see Regulatory References below

entry.core:emph: Ensure handover procedures for Senior Managers are in place and records are maintained of steps taken.
entry.core:para: Core SM&CR firms are not required to comply with the FCA’s handover rules, however, all firms are subject to SC1 of the Conduct Rules requiring Senior Managers to ensure that the area of business for which they are responsible is controlled effectively; in this regard the FCA suggests that handover procedures may be helpful in supporting an orderly transition between Senior Managers

entry.core:emph: Ensure the firm has a policy on handover procedures which details how the firm complies with the FCA’s handover procedures requirement

entry.core:para: (PRs do not apply to Limited Scope SM&CR firms or EEA SM&CR firms)

row.entry: Ensure PRs are appropriately allocated to the individual, who in practice, is the most senior person for an issue (and who need not be a board member) and who has the necessary skills and capability to carry out the role; a list of relevant PRs is set out in each of the sector specific Practice Notes above

Ensure PRs are only divided or shared in limited circumstances (eg as part of a job share) where it can be justified and firms can confirm that there is no gap, generally each senior manager will be jointly accountable for the PR
Reflect the PR clearly in the Senior Manager’s Statement of Responsibility

Ensure a Senior Manager is accountable for the firm’s performance of its SMR obligations, including compliance with: conditions and time limits on approval; requirements about Statements of Responsibilities; the firm’s obligations under FSMA 2000, s 60A (Vetting of candidates by authorised persons), and the provision of regulatory references, in accordance with PRA

Ensure each individual performing an SMF has an SoR; this is required in order for the Senior Manager to be approved. An SoR is a single document outlining the defined business activities and material risks for which a Senior Manager is individually responsible and accountable, under the ultimate accountability of a firm’s governing body (see Practice Note: SM&CR—Statements of Responsibility (SoRs))

entry.core:para: Ensure SoRs are clear and easy to follow in order that Senior Managers and others in the firm, and regulators who understand the type of business that the firm undertakes, but are not familiar with how the firm organises itself, can understand the responsibilities of the individual Senior Manager
Ensure the SoR focuses on what the Senior Manager is accountable for; it should not describe the Senior Manager’s competencies and skills or how the responsibilities should be discharged
Ensure the SoR does not refer to any other documents

row.entry: Ensure that where an individual performs multiple SMFs across different firms within a group, they have one SoR per firm

Ensure SoRs are kept up to date and submit a notification of a change to a Senior Manager’s SoR when there is a ‘significant change’ to a Senior Manager’s responsibilities/management arrangements of the firm (see examples of what is and isn’t a ‘significant change’ in SUP 10C.11.1 G–10C.11.35 G). This includes where a Senior Manager has a Prescribed Responsibility (PR) added or removed from their responsibilities, or where there is a change to how responsibilities are shared between Senior Managers
Ensure records of SoRs are retained to comply with COCON and SYSC requirements, which includes record-keeping in relation to their management of that business
Ensure Senior Managers are aware of FCA guidance in DEPP 6.2.9-E G on delegation

Record-keeping is not required to comply with the Senior Manager’s Duty of Responsibility, however, such records might prove relevant to demonstrating the Senior Manager’s compliance with their Duty of Responsibility

entry.core:emph: Ensure the firm has in place a comprehensive and up-to-date Management Responsibilities Map (MRM), which describes firm’s management and governance arrangements under the SM&CR, including the roles taken by the individual Senior Managers
Notify the FCA of changes to the MRM where there is notification of a change to a Senior Manager’s SoR or application for approval for an SMF, otherwise, the FCA need not be informed of changes

Where firms operate in a group it is inappropriate to submit one MRM for the entire group, as the SM&CR applies to legal entities individually. However, under the guidance of SYSC 25, a firm may share management and governance arrangements within the group; in such cases, submit an MRM which shows how such arrangements fit together within the group

row.entry: Identify those Certification Functions relevant to the firm; note that the Certification Regime applies to those employees who are not Senior Managers, but whose roles could pose a risk of significant harm to the firm, its customers or market integrity (see Practice Note: Certification Regime for SM&CR Banking and SM&CR Insurance Firms)

Ensure those staff who fall within the wide definition of ‘employee’ in SYSC 27.4.1G, including individuals seconded to a firm and contractors, but not Non-Executive Directors, are identified appropriately for certification

entry.core:para: The Certification Regime is subject to territorial limitation. With the exception of the Material Risk Takers CF, which applies without any territorial limitation, certify certification employees who:
—are either based in the UK (or spend more than 30 days a year in the UK), or
—if based outside the UK, deal with UK clients
‘Dealing’ has a broad interpretation in this context and includes having contact with UK customers

row.entry: Note, the ‘30–day rule’ (see Practice Note: SM&CR—essentials for banks and PRA-designated investment firms—Certification Regime—Exceptions to the Certification Regime)
Perform fitness and propriety assessments of certification staff at the point of recruitment or prior to the individual performing a Certification Function
Perform fitness and propriety assessments of certification staff annually (see Fitness and propriety below)
Issue a certificate to the employee where the firm is satisfied the employee has the fitness, propriety and skill to perform the relevant role
Note, a certificate is valid for 12 months beginning on the day it is issued

entry.core:para: Where a fit and proper assessment is carried out but the firm declines to issue a certificate, give the employee a notice in writing setting out:
—what steps (if any) the firm proposes to take in relation to the person as a result of the decision, and
—the reasons for proposing these steps

row.entry: In the event of a temporary absence of an individual performing a Certification Function which does not require a qualification, arrange for cover without completing the certification process for a maximum of four weeks
Retain records of every employee who has a valid certificate issued by the firm

Submit data on all certified staff as Directory Persons to appear on the Financial Services Register, see Practice Note: The Financial Services Register—Practicalities relating to reporting on Directory Persons—information reporting and time frames
Ensure a Senior Manager is accountable for the firm’s obligations of training and reporting under the Certification Regime in accordance with Prescribed Responsibility (B)
Ensure the firm’s fitness and propriety policy is clear, documented and implemented across all areas of the firm, including Human Resources (HR), Compliance, Legal departments etc

Ensure the process for conducting the annual fitness and propriety is clear and applied consistently; consider whether it is done through annual performance reviews or an alternative process. Ensure this is incorporated into the firm’s HR and other processes
Consider whether disciplinary processes and/or promotion processes incorporate fitness and propriety checks
Identify and train appropriate staff with responsibility for assessing others as fit and proper
Train senior managers and certified staff in the firm’s approach to fitness and propriety in order they know what the firm expects of them

Before making an application for SMF approval or issuing a certificate, ensure the firm is satisfied that the candidate is fit and proper to perform the relevant function, see Practice Note: SM&CR—FCA and PRA Fitness and Propriety requirements
Tailor a fitness and propriety assessment, in particular the competence assessment, to the specific role
Put in place development plans for any development needs identified as a result of fitness and propriety assessments
Ensure processes are in place for candidates considered to be ‘marginal’, this should include convening fitness and propriety panels, including senior managers, to review the assessment
Ensure processes are in place for candidates who fail fitness and propriety assessments

During the application process for an SMF, be prepared for the FCA to discuss the assessment of the candidate’s fitness and propriety informally with the applicant firm making the application; note, the FCA may retain notes of such discussions—see Practice Note: SM&CR—applications to perform SMFs, notifications, and withdrawal of approval

core:para.core:emph: Continuing assessment as fit and proper

row.entry: Ensure robust processes exist for continuing assessments so that at least annually, fitness and propriety assessments are undertaken for Senior Managers, Non-Executive Directors (NED) and certified staff (eg annual assessments)
Ensure clear processes are in place such that an assessment is triggered where events or information suggest concerns around fitness and propriety (eg in-year assessments)

When assessing continuing fitness and propriety, assess the role that the individual is actually performing at the time the assessment is done; ensure the assessor is provided with an up-to-date job description for that individual in advance of the assessment
Issue certificates of fitness and propriety to certified staff

entry.core:para: Notify the regulator in circumstances where the firm forms the opinion that there are grounds on which the FCA could withdraw its approval of an SMF holder; a firm should take into account how relevant and how important the matter is that comes to its attention before determining whether a notification should be made:
—submit Form D within seven business days of the firm becoming aware of information which may be material to the continuing assessment of an FCA-approved SMF manager’s fitness and propriety
—submit a ‘qualified’ Form C as soon as practicable, where a senior manager ceases to perform an SMF due to questions relating to their fitness and propriety
(see Practice Note: SM&CR—applications to perform SMFs, notifications, and withdrawal of approval)

row.entry: In considering the above, also consider the firm’s obligations under Principle 11 to report to the FCA and Fundamental Rule 7 to report to the PRA (see Practice Note: FCA and PRA enforcement essentials—preventing a referral to enforcement—Reporting to the regulator and third parties)

Ensure the firm is registered with the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS), or the equivalent agencies in Scotland and Northern Ireland, who run the criminal record checks. Smaller firms may need to use an umbrella organisation as an intermediary
Ensure criminal record checks are incorporated into the firm’s recruitment processes and procedures
Perform criminal record checks as part of checking SMF candidates and NEDs (where a fitness requirement applies) are fit and proper

Technically, criminal checks are not required for those carrying out Certification Functions. However, it would nevertheless be good practice to carry these out and many firms do so at appointment stage and thereafter on a semi-regular basis (see Practice Note: SM&CR—FCA and PRA Fitness and Propriety requirements—Fit and proper test—Criminal Record Checks)
Ensure fitness and propriety assessments, including the decision-making rationale and the outcomes are recorded and retained (see Regulatory References below)

tr:secmain.core:title: FS Register—Senior Managers and Directory Persons

row.entry: Submit all data on Senior Managers and Directory Persons to the FCA Directory using the FCA’s Connect system (for further information, see Practice Note: The Financial Services Register)
Ensure collaboration between compliance and HR, as HR processes must take into account regulatory reference requirements Ensure the firm’s recruitment teams understand these requirements
Ensure regulatory reference requirements are incorporated into the firm’s recruitment processes, including appropriate processes to obtain and provide regulatory references

Retain records of disciplinary, and fit and proper findings, going back six years (much of this information is also required to be retained as part of the firm’s statutory obligations to keep records for regulatory reporting)
Do not enter into arrangements that conflict with the firm’s disclosure obligations (eg non‑disclosure agreements)
Ensure Senior Managers are accountable for the firm’s regulatory reference obligations in accordance with Prescribed Responsibility (A) and Prescribed Responsibility (B)

Ensure compliance with the regulatory referencing requirements is consistent with the firm’s common law duties and other relevant legislation, such as those relating to the rehabilitation of offenders and spent convictions

Request a regulatory reference from all previous employers in the past six years for external candidates applying to perform SMFs, Certified Functions and non-approved NED roles (NEDs who are not Senior Managers)
For Senior Managers, obtain the regulatory reference no later than one month before the end of the application process
For Certified Staff, obtain the regulatory reference before issuing the certificate
Where it proves difficult to obtain a reference, such as from firms overseas, take all reasonable steps to obtain it

Where it proves difficult to obtain a reference, but the former employee is an authorised firm, explain the request is made under SYSC 22 and inform your FCA case officer (if you have one). Call the FCA helpline on 0300 500 0597 or email firm.queries@fca.org.uk
Where a candidate is/was employed by a non-financial firm, consider the general employment reference for any relevant information

Where an employee moves between group entities, a reference from the original entity is not required if the group maintains centralised records or alternative means of sharing existing relevant information on the fit and proper assessment of candidates; refer to SYSC 22.8A.3G to determine whether a reference is required from third-party (non-group) employers
Note, it is not necessary to request a reference from a candidate that was a sole trader
Respond to a request from a regulated firm (eg not a recruitment agency)
Use the standard template to provide the reference (see SYSC 22 Annex 1R)
Respond appropriately to a reference request within six weeks
Disclose information going back six years, including details of any disciplinary action taken due to breaches of the Conduct Rules and any findings that the candidate was not fit and proper

Disclose any other information relevant to assessing whether a candidate is fit and proper covering the previous six years (unless it relates to serious misconduct, in which case there is no time limit). An example of such information might include the number of upheld complaints, but the FCA says firms will need to use their judgement when considering what is relevant on a case‑by‑case basis
Properly verify any information that will be disclosed; information that a firm is not been able to verify, does not impose a wider duty on firms to investigate it

entry.core:para: Update regulatory references where:
—new information arising would have caused the providing firm to have written the original reference differently had the information been known at the time, and
—the new information would change an assessment of the fitness and propriety of the individual

The updating requirement applies to any notice period served between providing a reference and the individual leaving a firm and for ex‑employers, six years from the date the individual left the firm, unless the misconduct is serious

row.entry: Ensure the firm’s Conduct Rules policy is clear, documented and implemented across all areas and processes of the firm, including Human Resources (HR), Compliance, Legal departments etc (see Practice Note: Conduct Rules for SM&CR Firms)
Ensure the firm’s staff to whom the Conduct Rules apply are properly identified
Ensure those staff who fall within the wider definition of ‘employee’ to whom the Conduct Rules also apply, are identified
Ensure those employees who are not subject to the Certification Regime because they are an emergency appointment or are in a temporary UK role, to whom the Conduct Rules also apply, are identified
Identify the firm’s auxiliary staff to whom the Conduct Rules do not apply
Notify relevant staff that the Conduct Rules apply
Note, the Conduct Rules do not apply to the firm’s Appointed Representatives
Ensure a Senior Manager is accountable for the firm’s obligations of training and reporting under the Conduct Rules in accordance with Prescribed Responsibility B1
Take reasonable steps, including training staff, to make sure that relevant staff understand how the Conduct Rules apply to them in the context of their role. Consider bespoke training for each role
Ensure any role change involves further training specific to the new role
Monitor attendance at training, ensure anyone who misses training attends at a later date; consider incorporating attendance into performance reviews
Monitor trained employees to ensure compliance and allow reporting of breaches

entry.core:para: Report to the FCA disciplinary action against individuals who breach the Conduct Rules where the firm has:
—issued a formal written warning
—suspended or dismissed the individual
—reduced or recovered any of the person’s remuneration

row.entry: Notify the FCA of breaches by Senior Managers of Individual and/or Senior Manager Conduct Rules within seven business days of concluding disciplinary action using Form D (or Form C where the individual will no longer be approved). Where the employee appeals the disciplinary action, and the appeal is successful, the FCA should be updated as soon as is reasonably practicable after the appeal

Notify the FCA of Conduct Rules breaches by Certified Staff and other staff subject to the Conduct Rules, resulting in disciplinary action which has been concluded, on an annual basis (within two months of the end of the reporting period which runs from 1 September to 31 August each year), using form REP008 of the FCA’s reporting system, GABRIEL; this should include breaches by individuals subject to disciplinary action who have subsequently left the firm during the reporting period and breaches by employees who have appealed disciplinary action. Where an appeal is successful the FCA should be updated in the firm’s following REP008 form. Limited permission consumer credit firms will report in line with their reporting year alongside their annual return
In considering the above, also consider the firm’s obligations under Principle 11 to report to the FCA
Make an annual notification about Conduct Rules even if there haven’t been any breaches

Note, where firms wish to apply Conduct Rules to all of their staff, including ancillary staff, they may do so, but only those breaches by Certified Staff and other staff subject to the Conduct Rules should be reported
Keep records to demonstrate compliance with COCON, such as records of training given and any breaches, and the action taken
Those employees subject to the Conduct Rules should ensure they are aware of and comply with the rules as part of their job

tr:secmain.core:title: Senior Manager Task List
tr:secmain.core:para: Aside from the requirements for the firm, Senior Managers must themselves consider their personal accountability:

row.entry: Ensure they understand and are comfortable with overseeing an identified area of the business as set out in their SMF and/or their Prescribed Responsibility
Ensure their SoR is accurate and up-to-date. Preparing and maintaining an up to date SoR is a legal requirement for Senior Managers
Ensure they understand their Duty of Responsibility

Ensure they are confident that structures and processes allow them to effectively oversee their area of responsibility to prevent a regulatory breach—are there effective reporting lines in place? Ensure management information flows are in place so they can properly identify, assess and manage risks in the areas of business for which they are responsible, for further information, see Practice Note: Avoiding unwanted attention—how senior managers should fulfil their personal regulatory duties
Ensure they embed a healthy culture which aims to prevent misconduct and unfair treatment of customers, see Practice Note: FCA supervisory and enforcement focus on culture

Ensure that any delegation is reasonable, that the individuals to whom they have delegated are appropriate, for example with suitable skills, and retain an appropriate level of oversight (DEPP 6.2.9E sets out guidance on what the FCA consider to be reasonable steps in terms of delegation)

Note, Senior Managers may wish to keep records of relevant steps they take, in case questions are raised, whether by their firm, its lawyers, auditors, insurers or customers, the FCA or another regulator, for further information, see Practice Note: Regulatory action against Senior Managers
Ensure relevant staff are aware of and comply with the Conduct Rules and Senior Manager Conduct Rules as part of their job
Ensure key employment documents such as template service agreements and settlement agreements take account of a firm’s obligations under the SM&CR

Ensure HR policies comply with the SM&CR, for example, ensure they comply with FCA/PRA whistleblowing rules and allow firms to deal with any performance or disciplinary issues in relation to Senior Managers and certified staff

entry.core:para: Consider how a firm’s purpose, leadership, accountability, capabilities and incentives drive the firm’s culture and consider what changes are necessary to achieve a ‘healthy culture’, see practical guidance in: Culture and social governance in financial services—overview
